newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by continued large hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $51.00 to $51.50, with the possibility of extreme tops near $53.00, they said.
Illinois top prices at plants could range from $50.50 to $51.00, sources there said. Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant could range from $50.00 to $50.50.
Hogs also were coming in at heavier weights, which further weighed on pork prices as the supply pipeline filled.
Average Iowa/southern Minnesota barrow and gilt hog weights for the week ended Friday were 251.7 lbs, compared with 250.6 the previous week and 250.4 a year ago, USDA said.
Also, Friday last week USDA said the average weight of U.S. slaughter hogs at 253 lbs, up from 250 lbs the previous week but still below 256 lbs a year ago.
Carlot pork prices at midday were quoted mostly lower, with hams leading declines. There were 31.0 pork loads and 15 loads of trimmings sold, USDA said.
Losses Friday in hog prices could be stemmed if demand for Saturday kills is stronger than 35,000-to-40,000 head estimated by the trade, sources said.
